residual_defects_found_and_fixed.claim: The RAW8 (255) and 10-bit (1023) entries of RIGHT_JUSTIFIED_FULL_SCALES were unpinned. Removing 255 from the table left all 494 tests green.
residual_defects_found_and_fixed.why_it_matters: Both are real shipping containers, not theory: native/src/vendor/touptek.rs max_adu_from_bit_depth returns (1<<bits)-1 verbatim, so 8-/10-/12-/14-bit Touptek-family cameras declare 255/1023/4095/16383; QHY's container_max_adu(8, ..) = 255 and the SVBony RAW8 connect fallback also land on 255. It hardcodes the four containers rather than iterating the const, so dropping an entry fails the test instead of silently shrinking it.

alternatives_evaluated_and_rejected.idea: Count the pile-up across the whole tolerance band instead of only at the exact peak, so a clip smeared over several codes still counts.
alternatives_evaluated_and_rejected.rejected_because: It is the looseness the item warns against. Counting pixels >= clip_floor makes the test `is 0.05% of the frame in the top ~0.8% of its range?`, which a dim, noisy 16-bit frame whose peak happens to land in 4064..4095 satisfies from its noise tail alone (a 3-sigma tail is ~0.13%), redefining an ordinary frame's ceiling. Exact-peak counting matches the physics: a saturating ADC piles up on one code.

residuals_found_that_i_could_not_fix.claim: validate_image (the 3-arg validator used by api/imaging.rs:3667, :3797, :4106) has no percentage tier - only an all-or-nothing all_saturated check. A 70%-clipped frame is written to disk with no complaint on every container, including 16-bit. The resolved ceiling can therefore only ever change the verdict for a 100%-clipped frame there.
residuals_found_that_i_could_not_fix.why_not_fixed: Deliberate. The only consumer of those warnings is `tracing::warn!` - there is no user-visible surface - so adding a tier would ship exactly the disclosure-without-a-fix that this pass exists to eliminate. Recorded so the decision is explicit rather than an oversight.
residuals_found_that_i_could_not_fix.also: validate_image's low-signal check (fits.rs:1468) is still the unscaled `max_value < 100`, and cannot be scaled: for the inference to yield a ceiling the peak must already be >= 254, so the two conditions are mutually exclusive. Not a defect, a genuine limit of a validator with no sensor to ask.

non_defects_investigated_and_dismissed: 255's saturation threshold has only 1 ADU of headroom (254) because `>>7` truncates, and test_saturation_threshold_tracks_the_sensor_ceiling exempts it with `if full_scale >= 1023`. Looks like a disclosed hole, is not one: 1/255 = 0.39% is still 16x the largest documented real shortfall, an 8-bit container is produced by truncating the top bits of the ADC so it clips at exactly 255, and widening the band to 253..=255 would make 1.2% of all codes able to redefine the ceiling - the looseness the item warns against.
11-/13-/15-bit right-justified containers (2047/8191/32767) are absent from RIGHT_JUSTIFIED_FULL_SCALES. No such astro sensor exists; adding them would only add wrong-fire surface.

A left-justified frame can peak inside the 4064..4095 band (4080 = 255<<4) and have its ceiling redefined. Traced through: the consequence is only that the signal floor drops from 100 to 6 (Check 3 can then only pass more frames, never fail one) and that saturated_count covers the top 0.76% of the range, which stays under the 5% tier. The pile-up guard blocks it anyway - proven by the min_pile_up=3 sever above.

count_at_max counts only the exact peak, so a clip spread across per-column ADC offsets is undercounted. Worked the numbers: min_pile_up is 0.05% of the frame, so even a clip smeared over the full 32-ADU band retains ~30x the required pile-up.

first_pass_record.note: The prior agent's own report, retained in substance. Its claims were independently re-verified above; all held.
first_pass_record.residual_defect_found_and_fixed: The first fix taught only the BRIGHT end of the validator about the sensor ceiling; Check 3 (underexposure) still compared against a bare 100/500 ADU floor. On the SVBony RAW8 container (max_adu 255) 100 ADU is 39% of full scale, so every non-bias frame off that camera was called low-signal and any sub peaking under 100 was declared severely underexposed - an ERROR, which makes is_valid false, which makes unified_device_ops.rs return Err and destroy the frame. Added signal_floor_for_full_scale(), hoisted min(declared, observed) into `believed_full_scale` so saturation and underexposure share one believed container, and scaled Check 3's floor to it. Scaling can only lower the floor, so no frame that passed before can start failing.
caveats: `cargo fmt --check -p skotiq_imaging` reports diffs in imaging/src/stats.rs, another agent's file; fits.rs itself is rustfmt-clean.
No on-sky/hardware validation: the RAW8 path was reasoned from vendor/svbony.rs (container_max_adu -> 255 and the Raw8 -> u16::from widening), not against a physical SVBony camera.
